children: Novo Nordisk (NVO, Financials), is exploring the hair-loss market as the Ozempic and Wegovy maker looks to diversify beyond its blockbuster GLP-1 drugs.

Chief Scientific Officer Martin Lange said Novo could leverage its scientific expertise to move into hair loss, although the company has not decided whether to pursue the market first. The comments came as Novo outlined plans to find new growth areas beyond its weight-loss franchise.

Novo is targeting more than five drugs with multi-blockbuster potential by 2030 and expects more than $23 billion in risk-adjusted pipeline sales by 2035. The company also plans to pursue bolt-on deals and accelerate development of treatments for heart, liver and blood disorders.
The diversification push comes as Eli Lilly, has taken share in the injectable GLP-1 market and Novo faces a longer-term patent cliff for semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy.

Hair loss could offer a sizable consumer market. Pattern hair loss affects an estimated 50 million men and 30 million women in the U.S., while no new FDA-approved therapy for the condition has emerged since the 1990s, according to the report.
The next catalyst is whether Novo identifies a late-stage hair-loss asset or other consumer-focused treatment it can advance toward the market.

title: Novo Nordisk Just Made a Surprising Move Beyond Weight Loss
